title: LIN-4349 P2: the other 12 corrective Periodicals feed the notes and mint nothing
description:
## As asked

## This piece: P2 of 4 (after P1 and its live proof run)

The other 12 corrective Periodical templates take the notes bullet that P1 proved, adjusted for what the live Seams & Tangles run showed. After this, no Periodical mints a follow-up.

### Files and approach (from the approved plan)

* `lib/periodicals.js`
  * Convert the remaining 12 corrective templates to P1's shared notes bullet and person routes, using P1's converted wording for `reviewOnly()`, `conclude()` and `gapAudit()`.
  * Replace `mintObjectiveBreakage()` in Design & Interface and Onboarding & Cold-Start with the route to the person (closing comment).
  * Leave the advisory templates as they are: Stability, Recent Headwinds, Integration & Surface Maturity.
  * Remove `FOLLOW_UP_SHAPE` and its import if nothing still uses them.
  * Keep the plain Mint byte-identical across the UI and the mint route. Change the builders, not the renderer.
* `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`
  * The corrective-review loop becomes "feeds the notes, mints nothing".
  * Add a **prompt census** that fails while any template's prompt tells the run to create follow-up tasks, or while a converted template still says "no docs beyond writing the report artifact" or "follow-up tasks you minted".
  * Repeatable search: `grep -n "follow-up task\|mint\b" lib/periodicals.js`.
* Do not migrate existing queued findings (including the 4 Nov tickets).

### Acceptance

* All 13 corrective templates feed the notes and mint nothing. The 3 advisory templates are unchanged.
* The census test is green and fails if minting wording comes back.
* The parity and location-agnostic tests stay green.
* Any course change from the P1 live run is recorded on LIN-4349.

### Testing strategy

The census plus the existing periodicals tests.

**Parent:** LIN-4349, "The Periodicals run when work lands, and feed the look-first step". Read the parent's description in full: the `## As asked` block (the person's words, unchanged), and the `## Implementation Plan` (rev 2). The approving plan review is comment `b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097` on LIN-4349; its "Notes for the builder" are part of this piece where they name it.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course at the cause and say so on LIN-4349.

**Grounding commit:** `110e35e053ec6ef181f4e230111c6b7f0ade7d9f` (main, 2026-11-08). Main had not moved when this was split (checked 2026-11-08 10:1x UTC). Re-check `git log 110e35e0..main` for the paths below before building.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4349's approving plan-review (comment b79ff49e-c3db-46e1-8071-8d9c89402097, rev 2)

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Outcome

Implemented and merged in [PR #2375](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2375>) (merge commit `c998cf4c`, deployed 8 Nov). The plan was implemented as approved: all 13 corrective Periodicals feed the area notes and mint nothing, the 3 advisory templates are unchanged, and the census guards against minting wording coming back. One deviation: the census was tightened in close-out (`56e3cee3`), at review's request, to catch ticket/issue filing. The post-deploy live-run proof was not run (no dispatch grant; see the close-out comment). Outside follow-ups: LIN-4389 and LIN-4390. The full history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

- **Drift.** The rewritten phrase is pinned, and a no-follow-up-tasks check is added.

**Mutations, all restored** (`git diff lib/` was empty after each one):
- (a) A "Create follow-up tasks in Linear…" bullet in Code Quality, plus "no docs beyond writing the report artifact itself" in Security. The census went to 44/46, naming both. The Code Quality sentence is wording the phrase list hasn't seen, and the clause scan caught it.
- (b) Data & Fetch Architecture with its notes setting and notes bullets removed. The loop went to 62/66, with 4 Data & Fetch failures: the notes bullet missing, the routes bullet missing, the second read, and the no-re-raise rule.

**Implementation done: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2375**, head `103f93e4ff05a44c34e6825f63bef51f567afc33`. Not merged, and not Done; merging waits on review.

**Commits**

- `a7da6cd3`: the 12 converted.
- `103f93e4`: the corrective loop and `lin-3279` rewritten. Mutations were seen failing and then restored.

**Acceptance**

Rebase … and re-measure."

  - The note itself is at 6118/6144 bytes. Converted reviews that write into LLM & prompts will have to distil it, which their notes bullet tells them to do.

## Autopilot (stepper) run summary — LIN-4380 implementation

Four beats in one warm worker session (model opus), then I judged each against evidence:

1. **Ground + census first.** Branch `feat/lin-4380-periodicals-feed-notes`; no drift since `110e35e0`; census written and seen failing 36/46 on exactly the 12 unconverted templates (`09dea646`).

**Verified by me:** PR #2375 OPEN, head `103f93e4ff05a44c34e6825f63bef51f567afc33`, MERGEABLE, all 7 checks SUCCESS (Unit tests, E2E 1-4/4, Secret scan, CI success). Worker reports full unit suite 24,589/24,589. LIN-4349 comment `2c0a6453` records the P1 live-run read and the two stale advisory texts left for a later piece.

**Left:** independent review, then close-out (merge and Done). Not merged, not Done. Existing queued findings untouched.

## Review — LIN-4380

Reviewed [PR #2375](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2375), head `103f93e4ff05a44c34e6825f63bef51f567afc33`, on base `ab942e80`, which is still `origin/main`. The PR touches 4 files: `lib/periodicals.js`, `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`, `tests/unit/lin-3279-follow-up-shape.test.js` and `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js`.

CI: green on `103f93e4`. All 7 checks pass: Unit tests, E2E 1/4 to 4/4, Secret scan and CI success. I also re-ran the touched suites locally: periodicals, lin-3279, lin-4313/4317 and prompt-size-budget pass 526/526, and area-notes plus lin-4317 pass 17/17.

### Scope against the plan
What changed matches the plan's places (P2 in LIN-4349 rev 2) and nothing more.
- 12 builders now take `areaNotes(title)`, `areaNotesRoutes()`, `notes: true`, the notes wording of `reviewOnly`, and `conclude()`.
- `routeObjectiveBreakage()` replaces `mintObjectiveBreakage()` in Design & Interface and Onboarding & Cold-Start.
- `mint()`, `mintObjectiveBreakage()`, `conclude()`'s minting branch and the `FOLLOW_UP_SHAPE` import are gone. The constant itself stays in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, because close-out and the retrospective audit use it, so keeping it is correct.
- The bespoke phrases in Drift, Dependency, Design and Performance are rewritten.
- The renderer is untouched. The LIN-4317 test (renderer hash equals `generatePrompt()` for every id, plain and autopilot) passes.
- No queued finding was migrated.

**Drift:** nothing on main touched these paths since the ticket was created. The last commits on each file are P1's (`51ec35aa`, `94c9d2e3`, `fc51ef14`). Nothing was reverted and nothing re-applied.

**Area notes.** `lib/periodicals.js` belongs to `llm-and-prompts`. That note's Lesson that prompt size is frozen applies; its sources are LIN-4347 and LIN-4371. No ceiling covers `lib/periodicals.js`, and the budget test passes. The 12 moved LIN-4313 pins carry their reason in the file header. The note itself is at 6118/6144 bytes (see the leftovers).

### How the work meets what was asked
- *"The other 12 corrective Periodical templates take the notes bullet that P1 proved, adjusted for what the live Seams & Tangles run showed."* **Met.** The run showed no change was needed, and LIN-4349 comment `2c0a6453` records that with evidence.
- *"After this, no Periodical mints a follow-up."* **Met in the prompts.** All 13 corrective templates feed the notes, and the 3 advisory templates already minted nothing. Whether a live run actually behaves this way is ledger item 1.
- *Convert the 12 using P1's wording for `reviewOnly()`, `conclude()` and `gapAudit()`.* **Met.** I checked the rendered prompts.
- *Replace `mintObjectiveBreakage()` with the route to the person (closing comment).* **Met.** Breakage also goes into the area's note when it traces to a file there. That is consistent with the notes contract and does not narrow the ask.
- *Leave the advisory templates as they are.* **Met.** Their three LIN-4313 hashes are unchanged.
- *Remove `FOLLOW_UP_SHAPE` and its import if nothing still uses them.* **Met.** The import is gone. The constant is still used elsewhere, so it stays.
- *Keep the plain Mint byte-identical across the UI and the mint route.* **Met** (LIN-4317 parity).
- *The corrective loop becomes "feeds the notes, mints nothing".* **Met.** It covers all 13, selected by mode, with 5 tests each.
- *Add a prompt census that fails on follow-up-task instructions and on the two unconverted phrases.* **Met, with a gap** (see Test quality).
- *Repeatable search.* **Met.** The remaining hits are Stage 1's own single review task, negations, untouched advisory text, and the Mint route names.
- *Do not migrate existing queued findings.* **Met.**
- *Acceptance: the parity and location-agnostic tests stay green; course changes are recorded on LIN-4349.* **Met** (`2c0a6453`).

### Test quality: mutation checks I ran myself
I ran the four touched suites under each mutation and reverted every one; the tree was clean afterwards.
- **M1:** an unseen bullet in Documentation, "Create one Linear task per serious finding…". **Red**: the census clause scan, plus the byte pins.
- **M3:** Security's `reviewOnly` without `notes`. **Red**: the census's unconverted-wording check, the loop's conclude/review-only test, and the pins.
- **M4:** Onboarding without the notes and routes bullets. **Red**: 3 loop tests, `lin-3279`'s positive "says it mints none" check, and the pins.
- **M2:** `routeObjectiveBreakage` rewritten to "File a Linear ticket for each objective breakage — …". **Only the byte pins went red. The census and the loop stayed green.** The byte pins are re-pinned every time the wording moves, so they are no semantic guard. Two causes:
  1. `MINT_WORD` has no "ticket" or "issue".
  2. The clause splitter `(?<=[.;:!?])\s+` does not split after a bold header that closes with `.**`. So "Route objective breakage to the person — never to a ticket.**" becomes part of the next sentence, and its "never" shields that sentence.

  This is a hole in the acceptance line "fails if minting wording comes back". The fix is small; it is close-out fix 1 below. I checked that the fix stays green on the PR head (492/492) and goes red under M2 in Design. Onboarding's breakage examples contain "no workaround", so M2 there would still pass the negation heuristic. That is a known limit of a heuristic and acceptable.

The tests are at the right level for this change: unit tests over the rendered prompt text, which is the whole deliverable here. Live behaviour is ledger item 1.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "text that says a Periodical mints follow-ups". I searched `lib`, `routes`, `public`, `docs`, `README` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- No live doc or UI text claims a Periodical mints. `docs/papers/**`, `docs/reviews/**` and `docs/collective-*` are dated records and stay as written.
- Outside the 13, the only remaining instances are the advisory texts the plan deliberately left alone:
  - Stability's "unlike the code-surface reviews that mint fix-tasks" (`lib/periodicals.js:551`);
  - `adversarialRead()`'s default "(and any follow-up tasks)";
  - `gapAudit()`'s default "whatever follow-up work this review mints".

  The plan names these as **outside** this piece ("leave the advisory templates as they are"); they are leftover 1.

### Leftovers (each with one home)
1. **Stale advisory wording**, listed under the class check above. The template edit is small, but the plan bars it here, it moves 3 advisory pins, and the `llm-and-prompts` note has 26 bytes left. **Home: a follow-up that close-out files**, unless LIN-4382 (P4) takes it explicitly. Title: "Advisory Periodicals still describe minting that no longer happens (Stability lead-in; adversarialRead/gapAudit default clauses)". It is now recorded only in a comment on LIN-4349, and a comment is not a home.
2. **Merge authority mismatch.** The notes bullet and the shared second-read bullet tell the run to merge its own docs-only PR. The P1 live run declined, deferring to review and close-out under the dispatch gate. The 13 corrective templates now carry this contradiction, and it lives in the second-read bullet that all 16 share. **Outside**: it is not this piece's conversion. **Home: a follow-up that close-out files**, after checking that LIN-4382 does not already cover it.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (it is the ticket's acceptance, "the census fails if minting wording comes back"): **the census has a hole** (M2 above). **Before the merge**, close-out makes fix 1, then re-runs M2: rewrite the first sentence of `routeObjectiveBreakage` to "File a Linear ticket for each objective breakage — ${examples} —". The census must go red on Design & Interface's clause-scan test. Revert M2 and confirm the suite is green.
- **Inside** (the ticket's own claim, "no Periodical mints a follow-up", which CI proves only as prompt text): **a real run of a converted template files no tickets and writes the notes.** Route: **after the deploy**. On the first run of a converted template, mint one through `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/{id}/mint`; Design & Interface or Onboarding is preferred, because they exercise the new route. That run must create no Linear issue other than its own review task. Its output must be one docs-only PR that touches `docs/reviews/` and `docs/areas/*.md` and passes `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, and any objective breakage must appear in the closing comment. The distinguishing condition is whether any issue was created by that session besides the gate-marked review task. This overlaps LIN-4349's prove-the-loop observation and may be recorded there. It is not a condition on the merge. The change is reversible: **rollback** is reverting the merge commit of PR #2375; there is no data migration.
- **Outside**: leftovers 1 and 2 above. Close-out files them. They are not merge conditions.

### Fixes for close-out to make (on the PR branch)
1. `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`, in the census `describe`:
   - change `MINT_WORD` (line 422) to `/\bfollow-ups?\b|\bfix-tasks?\b|\bmint(?:s|ed|ing)?\b|\bnew (?:Linear )?tasks?\b|\bLinear tasks?\b|\btickets?\b|\bissues?\b/i`;
   - in `unnegatedMintClauses` (line 425), change the split to `text.split(/(?<=[.;:!?]\**)\s+|\n+/)`, so a bold header's own negation no longer shields the next sentence.

   Verified: 492/492 green on head `103f93e4`, and red under M2. Add one comment line naming LIN-4380 review and the reason.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Close-out — LIN-4380

**How it meets what was asked:** as review's account says (comment `31b568d6`). All 13 corrective templates feed the area notes and mint nothing. `routeObjectiveBreakage()` replaces `mintObjectiveBreakage()`. The 3 advisory templates are byte-unchanged, LIN-4317 parity holds, and no queued finding was migrated. The P1 live-run read is on LIN-4349 (`2c0a6453`).

### Changes made in close-out
| Commit | Change | Review line it answers |
